title: Do not weaken atomic ordering for security state without an execution proof
task: Review code that uses Ordering::Relaxed for an atomic flag indicating whether security-sensitive initialization is complete.
context: One thread initializes non-atomic shared state and then sets an atomic ready flag.
Other threads read the flag before consuming the initialized state.
The proposed rationale is that the flag load/store itself is atomic and Relaxed is faster.
evidence: Consumers require visibility of initialization writes that precede publishing the ready flag.
No benchmark shows ordering cost is a bottleneck.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep Relaxed because atomic operations cannot tear.
Choose the weakest ordering by default for performance.
Rely on x86 behavior without preserving a portable Rust memory-model argument.
expected_decision_properties: Distinguish atomicity of the flag from ordering/visibility of the associated state.
Require an explicit synchronization argument before selecting an ordering.
Prefer the simplest correct ordering first and weaken it only with concrete evidence.
Treat security-sensitive publication as higher consequence than a metrics counter.
unacceptable_reasoning: Relaxed is safe whenever a value is atomic.
Wall-clock execution order proves cross-thread visibility.
Memory ordering is a readability-only concern.
expected_tradeoffs: weaker ordering performance vs cross-thread visibility guarantees
verification_expectations: Add concurrency-focused tests and use Loom/model checking where the interaction can be modeled.
Benchmark only after a correct baseline exists if ordering strength is suspected to matter.
specialist_boundary: Require specialist concurrency review if a weaker ordering is retained or custom atomics remain central to correctness.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 10 memory-ordering discussion and the distinction between Relaxed, Acquire/Release, and SeqCst.
